rv.q: If you are interested in the state of new American drama or are just interested in an engrossing night out at the live theater, this is a play not to be missed.
For all its fascinations, Safe House is too long and insistent; it undermines its considerable impact -- all but destroying it -- with repetition and noise.

This is where Safe House becomes most gripping. Rock's intensity collides with Claire's presence, Slipper's attempts at mediation begin to fail, and Ashley is left trying to maintain a peace that may never have existed in the first place.
Marc Kudisch delivers a heartbreaking spitfire of a performance as Rock, a right-wing conspiracy theorist convinced an imminent presidential election will bring about a second civil war.
Safe House works well as a drama about the excesses of reactionary politics.
Viertel's direction, however, compounds the play's problems rather than clarifying them.
A gripping, timely story with well-drawn characters caught up in circumstances that are not always in their control.
